answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using proof-of-space storage. To anchor an identity, an agent commits dense lookup tables to dedicated hardware and proves continuous data retention at the dawn of each epoch, signing fast read proofs with a falcon signature. This forces adversaries to commit scarce physical storage capacity and sustained disk bus bandwidth per identity. However, I/O latency spikes and flash wear can trigger read timeouts, falsely rejecting honest agents.
